subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI config/security recommendations may mutate user config, and what confirmation, audit, and dismissal policy should gate those mutations?
rationale: The remaining work decides the security boundary for UI-originated config changes and how much authority login recovery guidance should have over auth-related settings.

options.title: Implement allowlisted recommendation actions
options.body: Approve a narrow reusable UI pattern for vetted config recommendations that routes through existing config validation and requires explicit diff acceptance before applying.

options.title: Keep recommendations read-only
options.body: Leave Control UI hardening guidance as text and docs only, avoiding UI-originated config mutation for auth/security settings.

options.title: Defer to CLI doctor flows
options.body: Make doctor or upgrade-scan the canonical fixer and have Control UI link users to that flow rather than applying patches itself.

recommendation.title: Implement allowlisted recommendation actions
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow reusable UI pattern for vetted config recommendations that routes through existing config validation and requires explicit diff acceptance before applying.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Control UI login recovery and Settings work makes this the strongest available owner for the product/UX boundary decision.
